title: The Kiln That Ate the Tiles
story: In the roof-tilers' guild, Cindermoss the Kiln Lurker curls inside the great oven and scorches part of every batch. Mr 6 marches in with a slate and a stub of chalk, because the guild can't rebuild the orphanage roof without knowing exactly how many good tiles they'll get. Cindermoss grins soot: 'Fire keeps forty percent of everything I touch.'
question: The tilers load 850 tiles into the kiln. Cindermoss scorches 40% of them, and then 15% of the surviving tiles crack while cooling. How many perfect tiles come out?
solution: Cindermoss scorches 40%, so 60% survive the fire: 850 × 0.6 = 510 tiles.
Then 15% of those crack, so 85% stay whole: 510 × 0.85 = 433.5 tiles.
Mr 6 chalks the answer: 433.5 perfect tiles.
praise: Taking a percent off was exactly the right move — the kiln just had a second bite to subtract too.
hint: Losing 40% means keeping 60%. Find how many survive the fire first, then take the cooling loss off that number.
victory: Mr 6 held up the slate and Cindermoss squinted at the decimal so long the fire went out. Now the lurker works as the guild's tally-keeper, and half a tile still counts.
imagePrompt: A soot-smudged ember creature coiled inside a glowing brick kiln while a brave numeral-six knight in a blue cape holds a chalked slate of percentages in the orange firelight.
